description: Microscopic audit of dipole cancellation and E3 collectivity in 144,146Ba

e1_cancellation_analysis.dipole_operator: D_z = e (N/A sum_p z_p - Z/A sum_n z_n) = e (NZ/A) (R_{p,z} - R_{n,z})
e1_cancellation_analysis.proton_driving_orbitals: pi(1h11/2) <-> pi(2d5/2) with Delta l = Delta j = 3 (positive dipole ~ +0.35 e fm)
e1_cancellation_analysis.neutron_driving_orbitals: nu(1h9/2, 2f7/2, 1i13/2) with Delta l = Delta j = 3 (negative dipole ~ -0.21 to -0.35 e fm)
e1_cancellation_analysis.net_cancellation_mechanism: At N=90 (146Ba), occupation of intruder nu 1i13/2 (v2=0.20) and low-Omega nu 1h9/2 (v2=0.40), 2f7/2 (v2=0.27) increases negative neutron polarization to match proton polarization, collapsing D0 from 0.13 e fm in 144Ba to < 0.01 e fm in 146Ba.

static_vs_dynamic_boundary.good_parity_condition: <0+| Q3 |0+> == 0 identically for all laboratory parity eigenstates; transition matrix elements <0+||M(E3)||3-> do not directly measure intrinsic expectation values.
static_vs_dynamic_boundary.gogny_d1s_pes: Bernard 2016 unprojected potential energy surface is extremely flat along beta3 (< 0.5 MeV barrier); ground state wave packet F(beta2, beta3) has broad zero-point octupole spread.
static_vs_dynamic_boundary.parity_displacement: Energy displacement delta E(I) = E(I-) - 0.5[E((I+1)+) + E((I-1)+)] in 144,146Ba is 600-800 keV at low spin, demonstrating octupole vibrational softness rather than rigid pear shape (< 50 keV in 224Ra).
